matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) and do not rotate it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you move a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.example: Rotating a diagonal stick from an X to become vertical, turning the X into an I.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalising a move, ensure the total number of sticks remains unchanged.
matchstick.example: Adding a new horizontal stick to a minus sign to create an equals sign without removing any stick from elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each stick relocation, check each character for validity.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from a V, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and check that the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation, before you output it.
matchstick.example: Accepting the equation "X = V + I" without checking that 10 ≠ 5 + 1.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals forming a valid X or V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to an X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X, leaving a single diagonal line, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one character to a different character, altering both; ensure that after the move both characters remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the solution requires changing two characters by moving a stick between them.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a numeral to another numeral but forgetting to adjust the source, leaving the source character invalid.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer to the puzzle.
matchstick.example: Providing the corrected equation but omitting the required "Correct version of the equation:" prefix.

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change from the original can be achieved by moving exactly one stick (no more, no less).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalising a candidate solution, compare the original and proposed equations.
matchstick.example: Proposing a corrected equation that changes two characters, which would require moving two sticks.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave an empty placeholder.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If a move involves taking the sole vertical stick from an I.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from an I without deleting the I character, leaving an empty space.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transformation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator (+, -, =), ensure the resulting operator is a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to an operator.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '-' to '=', resulting in a '-' (invalid) and a '+' (invalid) operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and assumes the resulting equation is correct without checking the numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After forming a candidate corrected equation, convert each Roman numeral to Arabic numbers and confirm that the equality holds.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may output the corrected equation but forget to include the required final line or use wrong capitalization/spacing.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with a line exactly matching "Correct version of the equation: <equation>", using uppercase letters and collapsing whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character without placing it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the stick you move; after removing it from the source, immediately place it onto a destination character, keeping the total stick count unchanged.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may move a stick from a numeral without ensuring the remaining sticks still form a valid numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Verify that after removing a stick, the source numeral still matches a legal Roman numeral shape (or is removed entirely if it loses all sticks).

matchstick.description: Proposed equation not reachable by a single stick move (multiple sticks changed)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may propose a corrected equation that would require moving more than one stick, violating the puzzle constraint.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compare the original and proposed equations character by character, ensuring only one stick's orientation and position has changed.
